title: Truncations and homotopy colimits
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let $E^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $\mathcal A$, with differentials $d^i:E^i\to E^{i+1}$ and $d^{i+1}d^i=0$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In the etale application, $T$ is a scheme, $T_{\Et}$ is its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and $\mathcal A=\Ab(T_{\Et})$, or $\mathcal A=\Mod(T_{\Et},R)$ for a fixed commutative coefficient ring $R$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Integers index cohomological degrees, with the shift convention $(E[1])^i=E^{i+1}$ and differential $d_{E[1]}^i=-d_E^{i+1}$.

For $n\in\mathbf Z$, the stupid truncations are the complexes
$$
 (\sigma_{\ge n}E)^i=\begin{cases}0&i<n,\\ E^i&i\ge n,\end{cases}
 \qquad
 (\sigma_{\le n}E)^i=\begin{cases}E^i&i\le n,\\ 0&i>n.\end{cases}
$$
Their differentials equal $d^i$ when both adjacent terms are retained and are zero otherwise. Thus $\sigma_{\ge n}E$ is a subcomplex and $\sigma_{\le n}E$ is a quotient complex. These are constructions on complexes, not in general functors on the derived category.

The good (canonical) truncations are
$$
 (\tau_{\le n}E)^i=\begin{cases}E^i&i<n,\\ \ker d^n&i=n,\\ 0&i>n,\end{cases}
 \qquad
 (\tau_{\ge n}E)^i=\begin{cases}0&i<n,\\ \operatorname{coker}d^{n-1}&i=n,\\ E^i&i>n.\end{cases}
$$
The differential into $\ker d^n$ and the differential out of $\operatorname{coker}d^{n-1}$ are induced by $d^{n-1}$ and $d^n$, respectively; all other differentials are retained or zero as appropriate. The induced maps of kernels and cokernels define these constructions on morphisms of complexes. They retain $H^i(E)$ for $i\le n$ and $i\ge n$, respectively, and have zero cohomology outside the retained range. Their images in $D(\mathcal A)$ are the truncation functors of the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category].

For $K\in D(\mathcal A)$, the successive-truncation triangle is
$$
 \tau_{\le n-1}K\longrightarrow\tau_{\le n}K
 \longrightarrow H^n(K)[-n]\longrightarrow(\tau_{\le n-1}K)[1]
$$
[lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]. Here $H^n(K)[-n]$ is the complex with its only nonzero term $H^n(K)$ in degree $n$. For bounded-below complexes and the left exact additive functors between Grothendieck abelian categories specified in [def-sp-truncation-couple], applying the derived functor to these triangles and taking cohomology constructs the truncation exact couple. In the cartesian-square, bounded-below setting of [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations], these are the triangles used for the hypercohomology filtrations. The individual triangle is not itself the bigraded exact couple.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with countable coproducts, and let $(E_j,u_j:E_j\to E_{j+1})_{j\in\mathbf N}$ be a sequence. Write $B=\bigoplus_{j\in\mathbf N}E_j$ and $\iota_j:E_j\to B$ for its coprojections; a coproduct is the colimit of the corresponding discrete diagram [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Define $s:B\to B$ by $s\iota_j=\iota_{j+1}u_j$. A homotopy colimit of the sequence is a cone object $H$ in a distinguished triangle
$$
 B\xrightarrow{\,1-s\,}B\longrightarrow H\longrightarrow B[1].
$$
We write $H=\operatorname{hocolim}_jE_j$ for such a choice; this triangle specifies the notion and does not specify a functorial choice of cones.

For a small category $I$ and a diagram $(F_i)_{i\in I}$ of abelian etale sheaves on $T$, its sheaf colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] is $P^\#$, where $P(U)=\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}F_i(U)$ is the objectwise presheaf colimit and $(-)^\#$ is sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification; lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact]. For sheaves of $R_T$-modules the same construction is performed in module presheaves, and its underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian sheaf colimit [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful].

For an abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\Et}$, if $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ is a geometric point, let $\mathcal N_{\bar t}$ be its category of pointed etale neighbourhoods [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods]. Then
$$
 F_{\bar t}=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal N_{\bar t}^{\mathrm{op}}}F(U)
$$
[def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], with the index category filtered by [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered]. For abelian sheaves, the stalk functor commutes with arbitrary small colimits and, degree by degree, with colimits of complexes [lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits]. For $R_T$-module sheaves this applies to the underlying abelian sheaves using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], with the induced $R$-actions. Colimits of complexes here mean termwise colimits in the category of complexes, not colimits in the derived category.

blueprint_update.statement:
For a complex $\mathcal E^\bullet$ of etale sheaves, the
*stupid truncations* $\sigma_{\ge n}$ and $\sigma_{\le n}$
are obtained by replacing the terms in degrees $<n$ (resp. $>n$)
by $0$. The *good (canonical) truncations* $\tau_{\ge n}$,
$\tau_{\le n}$ are the truncation functors of the standard
t-structure on $D(T_{\Et})$: they keep the cohomology objects in the
retained range and kill those outside it. The triangle

$$
\tau_{\le n-1}K\to\tau_{\le n}K\to\mathcal H^n(K)[-n]\to
$$

is the truncation couple of [def-sp-truncation-couple].

In a triangulated category with countable direct sums, the
*homotopy colimit* of a sequence $E_0\to E_1\to\cdots$ is
specified by a distinguished triangle

$$
\bigoplus_nE_n\xrightarrow{\,1-\mathrm{shift}\,}\bigoplus_nE_n
\longrightarrow\operatorname{hocolim}_nE_n\longrightarrow
\bigl(\bigoplus_nE_n\bigr)[1].
$$

The colimit of etale sheaves is the sheafification of the objectwise
colimit of the underlying presheaves. Geometric stalks are computed
by filtered colimits of sections over
pointed etale
neighbourhoods.
